title: When the gym is paused or its plan runs out, desk staff are told to download the data, which only an owner can do
what: The paused-gym message and the plan-ran-out message are shown to everyone at the desk. Both say you can still download your data (from Settings). Front desk staff never see the download card, because only an owner may use it.
expected: Staff are told to ask the owner; only the owner is told about downloading the data.
how_often: every time a gym is paused or read-only
fix_line: Give staff their own line: ask your gym owner

title: A locked-out owner's last way back in is an email that only one person can act on, with no record in HQ
what: An owner with no other signed-in device and no second owner is told to email MettleUp with gym name and mobile, and is promised a call and a code. That email lands in the general contact mailbox. HQ has no place to note the request or its state, nothing alerts anyone, and only MettleUp HQ can make the code. If that one person is away, the gym cannot open its desk.
expected: A locked-out request is logged and tracked like other support work, with a promised reply time and a second person able to make the code.
who: owners with one owner and one device
how_often: rare, but blocks the whole desk
fix_line: Track locked-out requests in HQ and give a second person HQ access

title: The data agreement tells the owner to open support access in Settings, but it is now in Help and feedback
what: The data agreement says MettleUp looks only in a window the owner opens in Settings. The MettleUp access card was moved to Help and feedback, so an owner who follows the agreement will not find it.
expected: The agreement names the screen where the card really is.
fix_line: Change the agreement line to Help and feedback

title: Help has no page on working without internet, and its forgot-PIN line names only one way back in
what: The offline front desk (look up members, take payments, then send them later) is live but no help page explains it. The staff and sign-in help page says only: where you are still signed in, make yourself a code. It leaves out the WhatsApp way, asking another owner, and emailing MettleUp, which the sign-in screen offers.
expected: Help covers the offline desk and lists every way back in that the sign-in screen offers.
fix_line: Add an offline desk help page and the full ways back in
